title: Private Deploy: Immutable upgrade artifacts and zero-trust network contract
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Deliver a concrete contract and acceptance criteria for Private/VPC deployments that enforces immutable upgrade artifacts, minimal egress (zero-trust) policies during upgrades, and verifiable offline/air-gapped upgrade flows. This ticket clarifies scope for engineering and security: what network endpoints we require, what artifacts must be signed and immutable, what rollback and verification steps are mandatory for customers running in VPC or air-gapped environments.
requirements: Artifact immutability: every release image and installer produced for Private must be signed (GPG or PKCS7) and content-addressed (SHA256) so that image hashes are the single source of truth.

Upgrade bundle contract: runtime images, k8s manifests, and optional sidecar images must be delivered as a single chained bundle (.tar.gz + signature) with a manifest that lists exact digests and required boolean feature flags.

Zero-trust egress policy: default upgrade path must succeed with outbound connectivity limited to a small allowlist of endpoints and ports. Any additional egress must be explicitly requested and logged via the Console and an operator-approved workflow.

Air-gap delivery option: customers can supply an offline bundle or we support a signed mirror payload that operators can pull via an allowlisted mirror. Provide clear fallback instructions and MD5/SHA checks for operators to validate artifacts locally.

Canary semantics for Private: provide a declarative canary window that runs new images on a configurable percentage of nodes; canary must include automated health checks, telemetry collection, and a fast rollback trigger if SLO regressions are detected.

KMS and key rotation: upgrades that change image provenance or signing keys must include a documented KMS rotation/rollforward path and an automated verification step that fails the upgrade on key mismatch.

Audit and telemetry: every upgrade operation must emit signed audit events (install start, pull success, verify signature, apply, health-check results, rollback if any) that can be exported to customer SIEMs or retained in our Console based on retention policy.

Compatibility matrix: the upgrade contract should include exact OS/kernel and container runtime compatibility constraints; upgrades must not attempt to change kernel-level requirements without an explicit major-version upgrade workflow.

Operator experience: provide a single CLI flow and Console-guided flow that performs all preflight checks (network, disk, KMS access, available node capacity) and outputs deterministic remediation steps.

Rollback criteria: automatic rollback must trigger if 1) >5% of requests fail within 5 minutes post-upgrade compared to baseline, 2) a health-check failure rate threshold is hit, or 3) a signature/manifest mismatch is detected.
Documentation: Confluence runbook, one-page cheat-sheet for air-gapped installs, and example iptables/ACL snippets for common firewall vendors must be published and linked by GA.
Security review: any deviation from the allowlist model requires Security signoff and documented compensating controls (e.g., TLS pinning, ephemeral credentials).
acceptance_criteria: A1: Engineering can produce a signed upgrade bundle with manifest that verifies locally (sha256 matches) and the build artifacts are immutable once published to the private-repo staging area.

A2: In a lab VPC with default-deny egress and only the approved allowlist (two endpoints + DNS over TCP), the Console-initiated upgrade succeeds end-to-end using the signed bundle and the cluster reports all signed audit events to the local audit collector.

A3: The air-gap flow: operator uploads signed bundle to an isolated cluster, runs the CLI preflight and apply steps, and the system verifies signatures, applies changes, and passes all health checks without external connectivity.

A4: Canary policy works: a 10% node canary runs for a 10 minute window, telemetry surfaces a regression metric, and engineering automated rollback completes and leaves the system in a healthy state with audit trail.
A5: KMS key rotation test: simulated rotation during an upgrade triggers the documented verification failure and prevents the upgrade until key reconciliation is performed.
A6: Documentation: Runbook, cheat-sheet, and firewall example snippets are reviewed by Security and Release Engineering and published under docs/private-upgrades by milestone delivery.
A7: Automated tests: integration test harness for private upgrades exists in CI that validates signing, manifest verification, and canary/rollback scenarios and is runnable by the release team.
A8: Security signoff: Security team approval recorded in the ticket with enumerated compensating controls for any requested non-standard egress rules.
A9: Console UX: operator receives deterministic remediation steps after failed preflight with links to the appropriate runbook sections and a one-click retry in the Console UI.

A10: Customer communication: template notification (email + Console banner) and incident prep checklist exist for customers opting into automatic upgrades and for those who opt for manual bundle application.
scope_changes: Initial scope included automated artifact mirror orchestration; out of scope for GA: managed mirror orchestration across customer networks. That will be tracked separately as PM-83021.
Out of scope: building vendor-specific firewall modules. Provide generic iptables/ACL examples only; vendor integrations are follow-ups.
Added during grooming: explicit KMS rotation steps and test scenarios after Security review request.
notes: Meeting 2026-03-04: Security asked for stronger audit events and signed telemetry — added to acceptance criteria.
We need ENG to prototype local signature verification tooling (lightweight) to simplify operator validation in air-gapped environments.
Follow-up: create PM ticket for managed mirror orchestration (PM-83021) and a design ticket for vendor firewall modules in Design track.
